ocaraka: ocaraka [fr. ocarati] in special meaning of one who makes himself at home or familiar with, an investigator, informant, scout, spy (ocarakā ti carapurisā C. on Ud 66). -- Thus also in BSk. as avacaraka one who furnishes information Divy 127; an adaptation from the Pāli. -- Vin III.47, 52; M I.129 = 189 (corā ocarakā, for carā?); S I.79 (purisā carā (v. l. corā) ocarakā (okacarā v. l. SS) janapadaṃ ocaritvā etc.; cp. K. S. p. 106 n. 1) = Ud 66 (reads coiā o.).
ocarati: ocarati [o + carati] to be after something, to go into, to search, reconnoitre, investigate, pry Vin III.52 (ger. °itvā); M 1502 (ocarati); S I.79 (°itvā: so read for T. ocaritā; C. explns. by vīmaṃsitvā taṃ taṃ pavattiṃ ñatvā). <-> pp. ociṇṇa.
ociṇṇa: ociṇṇa [pp. of ocarati] gone into, investigated, scouted, explored S I.79 = Ud 66 (reads otiṇṇa).
ocita: ocita [o + cita, pp. of ocināti1] gathered, picked off J III. 22; IV.135, 156; Sdhp 387.
occhindati: occhindati [o + chindati] to cut off, sever J II.388 (maggaṃ occhindati & occhindamāna to bar the way; v. l. BB. ochijjati), 404.
